sources.title: Driver Assistance Technologies
principles: Forward collision, lane departure, rear cross-traffic and blind-spot warning are driver-assistance functions; warning-only research must preserve the human driver's responsibility.
Research scenarios should distinguish warning behavior from intervention behavior instead of treating them as the same safety function.

sources.title: Automated Driving Systems
principles: Scenario research should explicitly represent system safety, operating conditions, object and event response, fallback behavior and human-machine communication.
Higher-automation safety guidance can still supply research questions for lower-level driver-assistance systems without changing KINGMAST's Level-0 production boundary.

sources.title: Enhanced Safety Vehicles crash-avoidance and mitigation research topics
principles: Safety research should combine virtual simulation or XIL with closed-track and on-road evidence rather than treating simulation alone as real-world validation.
Research coverage should explicitly include false-positive and false-negative behavior, vulnerable road users, motorcycles, intersections, nighttime, weather and challenging real-world scenarios.

sources.title: FMVSS No. 127 Automatic Emergency Braking final rule overview
principles: U.S. regulation places strong emphasis on reliable forward vehicle and pedestrian sensing.
KINGMAST uses this only as a scenario comparator for warning research and does not claim AEB compliance or braking authority.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/2144 General Safety Regulation
principles: The EU advanced-vehicle-systems framework includes intelligent speed assistance, driver drowsiness and attention warning, distraction warning and reversing detection.
Driver-monitoring data should be minimized and retained only for the necessary closed-loop purpose rather than continuously exposed or stored.
Concurrent driver warnings should be coordinated to avoid confusing duplicate prompts.

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1341
principles: Drowsiness warning validation should consider day and night operation and defined road/environment conditions.
Research should represent temporal evidence and uncertainty rather than infer drowsiness from a single frame.

sources.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1958
principles: Speed assistance may derive speed-limit information from signs, infrastructure signals, electronic map data or combinations of those sources.
Research must include incorrect, conflicting and unavailable speed-limit observations rather than assume the map or camera is always correct.

sources.title: Safe Driving 2026 protocols
principles: Modern assessment separates occupant monitoring, driver engagement and vehicle assistance while expanding virtual-testing support.
KINGMAST simulation should track driver-state, sensing availability and virtual scenario coverage as separate dimensions.

sources.title: UN Regulations 155 and 156 cybersecurity/software-update references
principles: Vehicle safety research should preserve cybersecurity-management and software-update traceability as independent assurance dimensions.
Simulation evidence must never substitute for cybersecurity management or update-management evidence.

sources.title: ISO 26262 road vehicles functional safety
principles: Functional-safety faults in electrical and electronic systems require a structured lifecycle and cannot be discharged by a perception simulation score.
The safety lab therefore reports research coverage separately from functional-safety compliance.

sources.title: ISO 21448:2022 Safety of the intended functionality
principles: Safety research should examine hazards caused by functional or performance insufficiencies even when no component has failed.
Unknown and difficult sensing conditions are explicit research targets rather than cases to hide behind a nominal pass rate.

sources.title: ISO 34502:2022 Scenario based safety evaluation framework
principles: Scenario-based evaluation provides a structured way to explore safety-relevant operating situations during development.
KINGMAST adopts only the public abstract-level concept as a research pattern and does not claim conformity to the paid standard.

sources.title: ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.9.0
principles: Static road geometry, lanes, road markings, objects and signals should be represented independently from dynamic traffic actors.
OpenDRIVE 1.9.0 is the current interoperability target for the independent safety lab's static-road bridge.

sources.title: ASAM OpenSCENARIO XML 1.4.0
principles: Dynamic maneuvers of vehicles, pedestrians and other actors should be described independently from road geometry.
The lab's native JSON scenarios are designed for reviewed conversion to OpenSCENARIO XML 1.4.0 without claiming schema conformance until externally validated.

sources.authority: National Assembly of Vietnam / Government publication
sources.title: Law on Road Traffic Order and Safety No. 36/2024/QH15
principles: Vietnam road-safety research must preserve local rule context such as lane use, speed, following distance and road-sign compliance.
The law's vehicle and traffic framework does not itself authorize KINGMAST road testing or automated control.

sources.title: QCVN 09:2024/BGTVT National technical regulation on safety and environmental protection for automobiles
principles: Vietnam's automobile technical-safety regulation is part of the production-readiness evidence landscape.
A software simulation result does not replace inspection, testing or certification under the applicable vehicle regulation.

sources.title: Model 3 Owner's Manual
principles: OEM driver-assistance documentation commonly describes feature limitations and degraded sensing conditions alongside functions such as forward collision, lane assistance and cabin-camera monitoring.
KINGMAST should explicitly recognize unavailable or blocked perception rather than silently treating missing data as safe.

sources.title: Toyota Safety Sense 3.0 overview
principles: A production ADAS pattern combines forward radar and camera sensing and explicitly scopes vulnerable-road-user and lane/sign recognition functions.
The independent lab should exercise sensor disagreement and road-user diversity rather than only same-lane passenger vehicles.

sources.title: BYD SEALION 7 safety and driver-assistance references
principles: Current OEM suites combine surround vision, driver monitoring, speed-limit intelligence, collision warning, cross-traffic awareness and blind-spot functions.
OEM manuals also document DMS limitations and retain driver responsibility, supporting explicit degrade/unavailable states rather than silent confidence assumptions.

sources.title: VinFast VF 8 new generation 2026
principles: A current Vietnamese EV benchmark combines highway assistance, adaptive cruise, lane keeping, blind-spot warning and 360-degree camera support.
This is a feature benchmark only; KINGMAST must derive its own logic and validation evidence rather than reproduce OEM implementation.
